frontier.hypothesis: A construct exists that injects an RA conflict at $a2 across the pointer's live range at ZERO instruction cost - the exact thing the original's RTL provably contained.
frontier.mechanism: The target reaches $a3 with only four block-locals, so under find_reg's ascending scan a fifth conflict at $a2 existed pre-RA and emitted nothing. Every honest construct measured so far either creates an instruction (dS4 +1, dZ +3) or is deleted before conflict construction (dead stores / named locals in jump1, aliases in cse, empty ifs in jump1, DCE-able duplicates in flow.c); the one post-local-alloc deletion channel that survives to conflict construction (cross_jump merging of identical arms) is structurally closed at both real branch sites (s12) and is a cheat when the arms are invented (Judge FAIL 2026-07-21).
frontier.next_probe: Do not re-probe arm duplication or five-local constructions. The productive lane is the operator-side Ruling C extension: add a HARD_CONFLICT_ADD atom class to tools/ra_solver/inverse.py and re-run --goal {"72": 7} to enumerate, typed, which single conflict additions reach $a3 and what RTL shape each requires. That is a tools/ edit, so it needs an operator or a session with tools/ in scope.
